Fresh owned private fleet-bucket backend supporting ordinary conditional writes and multipart; no real user bucket or cloud credentials entered here.
Two distinct R2 bindings in supplied config; per-case random key prefix independently witnessed empty; external limits and owned teardown mandatory.
cases.schedule: One active GET /case/I219; sequential awaited operations as written; all multipart handles and body readers stay inside this active request. I211 has at most six pages.
cleanup: After settled trace, finish/cancel every owned response body and finite input.
Abort any owned unfinished multipart upload before deleting keys; an active-request upload ID is never exported to another service.
Delete only registered synthetic keys; list both owned prefixes and require empty/nontruncated.
On unjoined trace or inaccessible reader, require external owned process/store teardown; never race cleanup against pending write.

cases.title: Resume an owned multipart upload within one live request
cases.intent: Resume an owned multipart upload within one live request
cases.failure_hypothesis: Same-node handle resumption may reference a different upload or lose original staged state.
trace: Create upload, retain its owned ID only inside this active request.
Resume using same binding/key/ID and upload final part.
Complete through resumed handle and read/head object.
cases.oracle: Resumed key/ID equal original; textresumed-final; size13.
cases.distinctness: Documented same-node multipart upload-ID lookup, not any retained stateless RPC capability or restart recovery.
cases.application_relevance: Upload handlers may resume a local active upload by its ordinary public upload ID.
